terra.problem: Isaiah is identified as a prophet and messenger without a reference supporting that fact. Isaiah 43:14 does not name him.
Babylon's status as a powerful kingdom is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The statement that the Jordan is a river is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The passage says the jackals and ostriches will honor the LORD; it does not say they watch His people drink.
The passage says the water is provided to give drink to God's chosen people, but does not say it cannot also be for the Chaldeans.
The explanation is flat and simply repeats the statement from the question without adding any personality or insight.
Saying the line is meant to be hard to hear assigns a purpose the text does not give, even though it is marked as Papa Dorin's thought.
Armies are mentioned in verse 17, but saying they were all over the first half stretches the passage.
Comparing the handling of Israel's sins to returning a burnt batch makes light of serious sin.
